reasoning.Student A:
My true preference is x > y > w > z. My priorities are w: 1, x: 2, y: 1, z: 2. Most applicants favor y > x > w > z.

I want to avoid dominated strategies. A ranking is dominated if there's another ranking that's always at least as good, and sometimes strictly better.

Let's consider my options. Since I have top priority at both w and y, I am very likely to get into either of them if I apply. Since I like x and y better than w and z, I want to apply to x and y first.

Consider the ranking y > x > w > z. I will propose to y first. If I get rejected, I will propose to x. If I get rejected, I will propose to w. If I get rejected, I will propose to z.
Consider the ranking x > y > w > z. I will propose to x first. If I get rejected, I will propose to y. If I get rejected, I will propose to w. If I get rejected, I will propose to z.

I have priority 1 at y. So if I propose to y, I will get in unless y is already full with people who like y better than me. Since most applicants favor y > x > w > z, this is unlikely.
I have priority 2 at x. So if I propose to x, I might get rejected.

Ranking x > y > w > z is better than ranking y > x > w > z. If I get into x, I am happy. If I get rejected from x, I will propose to y. Since I have priority 1 at y, I will get in. So I will get either x or y.
However, if I rank y > x > w > z, I will get into y for sure.

Let's consider other rankings.
If I rank w first, I will get into w for sure. But I don't want w.
If I rank z first, I will get into z for sure. But I don't want z.

Let's think about the ranking x > y > w > z.
If I get into x, great.
If I get rejected from x, I will propose to y. I will get into y.
If I get rejected from y, I will propose to w. I will get into w.
If I get rejected from w, I will propose to z. I will get into z.

Let's think about the ranking y > x > w > z.
If I get into y, great.
If I get rejected from y, I will propose to x. I might get rejected from x. Then I will propose to w and get in.
If I get rejected from w, I will propose to z and get in.

Since x > y, and my priority at y is 1, I should apply to x first. If I get rejected, I will get into y.

Therefore, I should choose x > y > w > z.
